html:
Hurricane Mitch was a huge hurricane that stalled over Central America in late October 1998. Its rains caused floods and mudslides that killed about 11,000 people, most of them in Honduras and Nicaragua.

Mitch moved slowly over Honduras for days. Rivers rose through Tegucigalpa, washing away whole neighbourhoods, and the north coast banana plantations were destroyed. Bridges and roads across the country were lost. In Nicaragua a crater lake on Casita volcano collapsed and buried villages.

It was the deadliest Atlantic hurricane since the Great Hurricane of 1780. Honduras's president said it had set the country back fifty years. Foreign debt relief followed, and the United States gave temporary legal status to Hondurans and Nicaraguans already living there, which encouraged a wave of migration north.
sum: Hurricane Mitch was a huge hurricane that stalled over Central America in late October 1998. Its rains caused floods and mudslides that killed about 11,000 people, most of them in Honduras and Nicaragua.
